nonClaims: NO ladder run and NO Playwright run happened in this lane. The pin proves the plan's environment object and the config's source text; it does not prove Playwright spawned a server with the key. Only a real authority-recovery run does, and the parent owns that proof.

The arm's EFFECT depends on U15a being merged. U15a (46de0b2f137d5c6f32f4637caad4c49c0aeaa276) is not an ancestor of this baseline, so on main today MEKSTATION_E2E_COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE reaches server.js and nothing reads it: COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE is still the literal 'off' at src/lib/multiplayer/server/matchJournalAuthority.ts:18. This unit forwards an inert key until U15a lands.

The cutover itself is NOT done. The production constant is untouched by this unit (no src/ file was edited at all), and the arm only fires under NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE, which only playwright.config.ts's own webServer sets.
No claim that the E2E-01/02 genesis clauses are proved. This unit makes them REACHABLE once U15a merges; proving them is the parent's main-proof run.

The playwright.config.ts pin is a TEXT pin over the source, not a behavioral one. It asserts both key names appear and that the combat key sits inside the same `...(process.env.<KEY> ? { <KEY>: process.env.<KEY> } : {})` guard the campaign key uses. It cannot observe the env Playwright actually builds. The config is not imported under jest because it is an ESM TypeScript module that imports @playwright/test and derives a per-run port and runtime directory at load time; that cost is the reason for the text pin, and this is the receipt saying so out loud.

The `authority` and `all` expansions now arm combat journal authority for every spec in those composites, not only E2E-01/02. That blast radius is inherited from the existing campaign-key condition, not introduced by this unit, but it is real and is not claimed to be scoped.

The 'leaves both journal keys off a group that does not arm the fixture' case was already green on the red run (vacuously - no group set the combat key at all). It is a mutant guard, not red evidence, and the red receipt records it that way.
npx oxlint on the two script files is vacuous: oxlint reported `on 0 files` because scripts/ is ignored by the root lint config. No lint opinion was obtained on those two files.

findingsReportedNotFixed.finding: The combat arm value 'enabled' is hardcoded in the ladder plan. There is no ladder selector for a 'shadow' run, so the compare-only mode U15a's resolver accepts is unreachable from the QC runner. If a shadow-parity ladder run is ever wanted, it needs a plan-level knob; adding one now would widen this unit.

Neither the plan nor the config validates the combat key's value. The QC runner always sets 'enabled', but the config forwards whatever is in process.env, so a hand-set MEKSTATION_E2E_COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE=on reaches the server and (per U15a's charter) resolves silently to 'off'. A misconfigured arm is silent. U15a's own receipt records the same finding on the resolver side; a value guard belongs in one place, not two.

`armsJournalAuthorityFixture` is now the arming condition for two different subsystems' fixtures under one name that still reads campaign-shaped. A third key on the same condition would make the name actively misleading. Renaming it is a pure-rename diff that would touch no behavior, but it is outside this unit's sentence.

The regex in the config text pin is whitespace-tolerant so oxfmt may rewrap the guard, but it is still coupled to the `...(x ? {k: x} : {})` spelling. A future refactor to, say, a small `forwardIfPresent()` helper in the config would go red on a correct change. The comment in the pin says it is a text pin; this records the specific brittleness.

U15a is owner-gated on packet PK-u15a-ruling (authority review class). U15b's own review class is routine, so nothing blocks this PR - but merging U15b while U15a waits on that ruling leaves main carrying a forwarded key with no reader. The parent should sequence the two, or accept the inert interval knowingly.
